_comment: The six questions, and the only place their wording is decided.
Before this file existed the homepage asked six questions, Ethicare Move
answered four, and only ONE of them was worded the same way on both:
'Can I register?' against 'Can I work there?', 'Could we afford it?'
against 'Can we afford it?' — one word apart, which reads worse than being
plainly different because it looks as though nobody checked. The same
question also pointed at two different pages depending on which surface you
arrived from. Roughly sixty pages quote one wording or another.
So: one wording, one destination, one call to action per question.
tools/sync-questions.py rewrites every page from this file and fails the
build if a variant creeps back in.
The I/we split is deliberate and worth keeping. 'I' is the clinician's own
career — whether they can work, what they would earn, what roles exist.
'We' is the household — what it costs, where to live, how to plan it.
A doctor decides the first three on their own; nobody decides the last
three without the person they live with.
href is where the question goes from anywhere on the site. href_move is the
exception: on /move itself, 'How do we plan it all?' cannot link to /move,
so it points at the guide library instead — the question is canonical, the
destination adapts to where the reader already is.
29 Sep 2026 — the JOURNEY. The site had three versions of it: the eight-stage band on the
guide pages, the six questions, and the master brief's Journey A, in two different orders.
One rule now: the eight stages are the journey, in the master brief's order, and wherever a
stage IS a question it carries the question's exact wording. The six questions are stages
3 to 7, with stage 4 (Make the numbers work) holding two of them. 'here'/'there' is the
deixis rule below: 'here' inside a country's guide set, 'there' everywhere else.
tools/sync-questions.py writes the band on every guide page, journey.js (what the tools and
the answers strip read), and checks move-steps and the Stage 0N references against this.

questions.sub: Registration, standing, English, character and health — and the tool that maps your route.
questions.sub_long: Every gate between you and practising: your regulator and the route most likely to apply to you, plus the standing, English, character and health requirements that actually set the timeline.
questions._note: Points at the hub rather than straight at /pathway-checker. The checker answers one gate — which registration route you are on. The question is bigger than that: certificates of good standing, English, criminal history, fitness to practise. Sending people to the tool first meant they met their route without ever meeting the things that delay them. The checker is the first thing on the hub.

questions.sub: Indicative pay, and how the agreements set it.
questions.sub_long: What the collective agreements actually pay, what varies on top of the scale, and what the tax and the cost of living do to it once you are there.

questions.sub: A real estimate of what the move costs.
questions.sub_long: Registration, visas, flights, shipping, temporary accommodation and the bond — what the whole move costs, what an employer usually covers, and what you need in the bank before you fly.

questions.sub: Cities and regions, and the trade-offs between them.
questions.sub_long: Two countries, thirty-three destinations, and an honest account of the trade-offs rather than a brochure. Written for the whole household, not just the clinician.

questions.sub: Live roles and the professions we recruit.
questions.sub_long: The roles we are recruiting now, the professions we cover, and the ones we are honest about not covering yet.

questions.q: How do we plan it all?
questions.sub: One plan for registration, visa, money and the first month.
questions.sub_long: Registration, the job, the visa, the money, the move and your first month, put in the order they actually happen — with a note of what you have already done.

variants.How do I organise it?: How do we plan it all?

deixis_rule: There and here are not the same word and the difference carries meaning. 'Can I work there?' is the canonical question, asked before the reader has picked a country — it appears on the homepage and on /move and goes to the pathway checker. 'Can I work here?' is stage four of the eight-stage journey band, which only ever appears INSIDE a country's guide set, where 'here' means that country — it goes to that country's registration guide, which is itself titled 'Can I work in New Zealand?' or 'Can I work in Australia?'. The two never appear on the same page, so a reader meets one or the other, never both. Anywhere else, 'Can I work here?' is drift and sync-questions.py flags it.
